# ggguides

*rearranging the legends on a ggplot*

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/gcol33/ggguides/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/gcol33/ggguides/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/gcol33/ggguides/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/gcol33/ggguides)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/ggguides)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=ggguides)
<!-- badges: end -->

ggguides places, styles and combines the legends of [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org) plots with named functions, such as `legend_left()`, `legend_inside()` or `legend_style()`, each added to a plot with `+`.

Each function sets the ggplot2 theme and guide options that belong to one change together, for a legend on the left its position, its justification and the alignment of the legend boxes, and returns an ordinary ggplot2 component that combines with the rest of the plot's theme. For layouts of several plots, `collect_legends()` and `shared_legend()` edit the gtable, the table of graphical objects that ggplot2 draws, so that one legend remains. You choose where each legend goes and how it looks, one aesthetic at a time when a plot has several. ggguides supports:

- **Placement.** `legend_left()`, `legend_right()`, `legend_top()` and `legend_bottom()` move the legend to a side, [`legend_inside()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/reference/legend_inside.html) into a corner or to `x`/`y` coordinates, and `legend_none()` removes it.
- **Styling.** [`legend_style()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/reference/legend_style.html) sets size, font, background, border and margins. `legend_wrap()` arranges the keys in columns or rows, `legend_reverse()` and `legend_order()` set the order of the entries, and `colorbar_style()` styles continuous scales.
- **Several legends on one plot.** The `by` argument of every placement and style function targets one aesthetic. `legend_hide()` and `legend_select()` drop or keep legends by aesthetic, and `legend_order_guides()` sets their order.
- **One legend for several plots.** `collect_legends()` and `collect_axes()` remove duplicates from a [patchwork](https://patchwork.data-imaginist.com) layout, `shared_legend()` arranges plots with one legend without patchwork, and `get_legend()` extracts a legend for [cowplot](https://wilkelab.org/cowplot/) or grid.

## Installation

```r
install.packages("ggguides")
```

Development version:

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("gcol33/ggguides")
```

## Usage

1. Build the plot with ggplot2.
2. Add a placement function such as `legend_left()` or `legend_inside()`.
3. Add `legend_style()` to change how the legend looks.

```{r left, fig.alt = "Scatter plot of car weight against fuel economy from mtcars, points coloured by number of cylinders, with the colour legend on the left of the panel."}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggguides)

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3)
p + legend_left()
```

Inside the panel, a corner is named with `position`, and the style is added as a further layer:

```{r inside, fig.alt = "The same scatter plot with the colour legend inside the panel in the top-right corner, its title in bold and its text larger."}
p +
  legend_inside(position = "topright") +
  legend_style(size = 18, title_face = "bold")
```

## Compared with theme()

In ggplot2, a legend on the left with its keys aligned at the top takes three `theme()` arguments. `legend_left()` sets them together:

```r
p + theme(legend.position = "left",
          legend.justification.left = "top",
          legend.box.just = "left")

p + legend_left(justification = "top")
```

## Several legends on one plot

A plot with several aesthetics has one legend per aesthetic. The `by` argument places or styles one of them and leaves the others as they are:

```{r by, fig.alt = "Scatter plot of car weight against fuel economy with points coloured by cylinders and sized by horsepower; the colour legend is above the panel and the size legend to its right."}
q <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt, colour = factor(cyl), size = hp)) +
  geom_point()
q + legend_top(by = "colour") + legend_right(by = "size")
```

Calls with `by` add up, one line per legend and setting. [Multiple Legends](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/articles/multiple-legends.html#six-legends-stacked-per-side) builds this plot with six legends, two on top, two on the right, one at the bottom and one on the left:

```{r six-legends, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.height = 6.5, fig.alt = "Scatter plot of car weight against fuel economy with six legends: colour and fill above the panel, size and transparency on the right, shape below and line type on the left."}
p6 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) +
  geom_smooth(aes(linetype = factor(vs)), method = "lm", se = FALSE,
              colour = "grey40") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = factor(cyl), fill = factor(gear), size = hp,
                 alpha = qsec, shape = factor(am)),
             stroke = 1.2) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 24)) +
  labs(colour = "Cyl", fill = "Gear", size = "HP",
       alpha = "QSec", shape = "AM", linetype = "VS")

p6 +
  legend_top(by = "colour") + legend_top(by = "fill") +
  legend_right(by = "size") + legend_right(by = "alpha") +
  legend_bottom(by = "shape") + legend_left(by = "linetype") +
  legend_style(by = "colour", justification = "left") +
  legend_style(by = "fill", justification = "right") +
  legend_style(by = "size", justification = "top") +
  legend_style(by = "alpha", justification = "bottom") +
  legend_style(by = "shape", justification = "center") +
  legend_style(by = "linetype", justification = "center") +
  legend_style(by = "colour", title_face = "bold", title_position = "top",
               key_width = 0.4, key_height = 0.4) +
  legend_style(by = "fill", title_face = "bold", title_position = "top",
               key_width = 0.4, key_height = 0.4) +
  legend_style(by = "size", title_size = 14) +
  legend_style(by = "alpha", title_size = 14) +
  legend_style(by = "shape", direction = "horizontal") +
  legend_style(by = "linetype", direction = "vertical") +
  legend_style(by = "colour", margin = c(0, 0, 0.2, 0)) +
  legend_style(by = "fill", margin = c(0, 0, 0.2, 0)) +
  legend_style(by = "size", margin = c(0, 0, 0, 0.3)) +
  legend_style(by = "alpha", margin = c(0, 0, 0, 0.3)) +
  legend_style(by = "shape", margin = c(0.3, 0, 0, 0)) +
  legend_style(by = "linetype", margin = c(0, 0.3, 0, 0))
```

## One legend for several plots

A patchwork layout repeats the legend of each plot. `collect_legends()` keeps one, and `span = TRUE` stretches it along the full height of stacked plots:

```{r collect, fig.height = 8, fig.alt = "Three scatter plots of mtcars stacked vertically, of weight, horsepower and displacement against fuel economy, with one colour legend for cylinders on the right spanning all three panels."}
library(patchwork)

p1 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt, colour = factor(cyl))) + geom_point()
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, hp, colour = factor(cyl))) + geom_point()
p3 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, disp, colour = factor(cyl))) + geom_point()
stacked <- (p1 / p2 / p3) + plot_layout(heights = c(2, 1.5, 1))

gt <- collect_legends(stacked, position = "right", span = TRUE)
grid::grid.draw(gt)
```

With `span = 1:2` the legend sits beside rows 1 and 2 only. Without patchwork, `shared_legend(p1, p2, p3, ncol = 1, position = "bottom")` arranges the plots with one legend. [Patchwork Integration](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/articles/patchwork.html) covers both, along with collected axes and cowplot.

## Documentation

Start with [Getting Started with ggguides](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/articles/getting-started.html): placing, styling and wrapping a legend, and combining the functions on one plot.

- [Legend Positioning](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/articles/positioning.html): the four sides, positions inside the panel, direction and removing the legend.
- [Styling & Customization](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/articles/styling.html): fonts, text rotation, backgrounds, borders, key size, wrapping, entry order and colour bars.
- [Multiple Legends](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/articles/multiple-legends.html): hiding, selecting, ordering, merging and placing legends per aesthetic.
- [Patchwork Integration](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/articles/patchwork.html): one legend and shared axes across a layout of plots.
- [Full reference](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/reference/): every function, grouped by job.

## Getting help

Questions and bug reports go to the [GitHub issues](https://github.com/gcol33/ggguides/issues). A bug report is easiest to act on with a small reproducible example, for instance made with [reprex](https://reprex.tidyverse.org/).

```{r citation, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cit <- citation("ggguides")
fence <- function(lang, x) cat("```", lang, "\n", paste(x, collapse = "\n\n"), "\n```\n\n", sep = "")
cat(attr(cit, "mheader"), "\n\n", sep = "")
fence("text", format(cit, style = "text"))
cat("BibTeX:\n\n")
fence("bibtex", format(cit, style = "bibtex"))
```
